title.narrative: Rapid Response to Support the Humanitarian Crisis in Sudan, Phase III

description.narrative: ltpgtSince 2012, Saferworld has engaged with and supported 50+ National Non-Governmental Organisations (NNGOs) and informal community groups (such as women- and youth-led associations) to enhance their capacities to strengthen peaceful coexistence, social cohesion, and positive conflict transformation across Khartoum, Darfur, Eastern Sudan, West and South Kordofan and Blue Nile, including in SPLM-N controlled areas. ltbrgtOver the last three years, Saferworld Sudan has been supporting NNGO partners to strengthen the autonomous pro-peace initiatives of local communities using the rushash approach, which involves providing small and micro-grants to NNGO partners and community groups to enable rapid community-led response to peacebuilding, conflict prevention and transformation. Since the outbreak of the conflict in Sudan, Saferworld has been working with NNGOs, emergency response rooms (ERRs), women, and youth groups (referred to collectively in this proposal as Mutual Aid Groups, or MAGs) to support humanitarian and conflict prevention activities – including with funding from Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF). ltbrgtSince July 2023, with funding from SHF, Saferworld has worked with 20 Sudanese NNGOs in Phase I (July 2023 – June 2024) and 25 NNGOs in Phase II (August 2024 to-date) to support initiatives led by youth and women in Khartoum, Sinnar, Eastern Sudan (all three states), South Kordofan (both sides of the conflict divide), West Kordofan and Blue Nile, using its proven rushash approach. In Phase I, a total of over USD 1,719,000 was transferred to MAGs through NNGO partners to support humanitarian and conflict prevention activities, provide dignity kits for women, life-saving water, food, essential medicines, and non-food items to internally displaced people, and to facilitate the relocation of communities attacked by parties to the conflict to safer arears, among others. In Phase II, at least USD 1,790,000 has been allocated. Of this, USD 1,640,000 has been transferred and USD 150,000 committed to MAGs, while USD 1,154,475 is programmed for MEL, operations and personnel costs. Since Phase One started, more than 500,000 people have been reached with life-saving humanitarian support. Saferworld’s staff on the ground have led in monitoring project activities, worked closely with partners to ensure that the risk of aid diversion is reduced and that project activities do not inadvertently support parties to the conflict. ltbrgtKey successes in the first phase include: establishment of a localisation coordination council (LCC) which brings together Khartoum, Sinnar, Darfur ERRs and Saferworld partners to review needs, coordinate rapid responses and strengthen mutual and community accountability and to provide effective support to local initiatives across the country to address a multiplicity of needs of host communities and IDPs, and that strengthen peaceful co-existence and social cohesion. This integrated humanitarian, development, peace (HDP) nexus approach is critical for reinforcing community peace in the face of ethnic and tribal divisions, and to support access, strengthen social protection and resilience. This project will continue to adapt the rushash approach to enable NNGOs (and in some cases, Saferworld staff directly), to support existing community-embedded MAGs to strengthen and sustain the impacts of their response to the crisis. In our consultations with them, MAGs have recommended that the average microgrant amount remains USD 3,000. In Phase III, Saferworld will partner with 20 NNGOs from the second phase, of which at least 25% will be women-led organisations (WLOs). Between them they will receive between $30,000 and $160,000 in funding. We will maintain a dynamic and flexible approach to small-granting and will adopt a deliberate approach to reach more women led organisations and groups (at least 20% of micro grants will go to women-led groups) and to integrate a gender responsive/transformative approach in all activities. lt/pgt
